Hlabisa warns of extreme heat and drought risks this summer
Saturday 17 October 2026 - 11:50am
JOHANNESBURG - Cooperative Governance Minister Velenkosini Hlabisa warns that this summer will bring tough weather, with soaring temperatures and heatwaves expected under El Niño.
He said government is activating disaster management systems and ramping up communication to help communities prepare for droughts and other weather risks.
Hlabisa spoke during the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction programme in Mpumalanga, which focuses on building resilience and ensuring communities know how to respond when disasters strike.
"Not only this weekend, from this summer season up to March 2027, the most difficult weather conditions under El Nino, the high temperature, but high levels of heat is also going to be a disaster that we are talking about activating our systems, ensuring communication reaches everybody, because we should be ready to mitigate the effects of drought that will be as a result of the heat waves, our farmers, our children at schools, in homes that people must not expose themselves unnecessarily."

Heat Advisory continues until 8 pm on Saturday, much cooler next week
Red Flag Warnings end at 6 pm, but gusty winds are still expected across mainly the higher elevations. Heat Advisory continues until 8 pm on Saturday; much cooler next week with scattered showers
Here is your Central Coast weather forecast for San Luis Obispo County and Santa Barbara County from Meteorologist Jim Castillo
Mountain & Foothill Wind Speeds
Red Flag Warnings end at 6 pm but gusty winds are still expected across the Santa Lucia Mountains, Santa Ynez Mountains, and the Los Padres National Forest sections of both counties.
Coastal & Inland Wind Speeds
Weaker winds across lower elevations, coastal areas, and non-traditional wind corridors.
Temperature & Heat Risk
Highs stretching from the mid-80s to mid-90s across coastal plains and coastal valleys Saturday, creating moderate to locally major heat risk.
Heat Advisory remains in effect across coastal and valley areas through Saturday.
Cooling Trend
Onshore wind flow returns Sunday into Monday, dropping daytime highs significantly down to the 70s area-wide by Monday and 60s on Tuesday.
Midweek Rain Potential
Increasing confidence for light scattered rain starting late Tuesday, with a better chance Wednesday, and initial projections bringing some measurable rainfall across both counties.
